FAQ.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
FAQ.subtitle: Everything you need to know about Mdmak Tech
FAQ.q1: How does Mdmak Tech connect contractors with suppliers in Saudi Arabia?
FAQ.a1: Mdmak Tech is a B2B procurement platform where contractors post RFQs, and verified suppliers submit competitive quotes. The platform streamlines the entire sourcing process — from posting requirements to comparing offers and awarding contracts — all in one place.
FAQ.q2: Is Mdmak Tech free to use?
FAQ.a2: Yes, contractors and suppliers can register and start using the platform for free. The Starter plan includes up to 5 RFQs per month with basic quotation features. For higher volumes and advanced features, we offer Pro and Enterprise plans.
FAQ.q3: What construction materials can I source through the platform?
FAQ.a3: You can request quotes for a wide range of construction materials including steel, cement, electrical supplies, paints, sanitary ware, HVAC systems, insulation, flooring, doors, and more. The platform supports all major categories used in Saudi construction projects.
FAQ.q4: How quickly do suppliers respond to RFQs?
FAQ.a4: Suppliers are notified instantly when a new RFQ is published. Response times vary, but most suppliers submit their offers within 24-48 hours. The platform sends automatic reminders as the deadline approaches to ensure competitive participation.
FAQ.q5: Can Mdmak Tech handle large-scale construction projects?
FAQ.a5: Absolutely. Mdmak Tech is built for projects of all sizes — from small renovations to large-scale commercial and infrastructure developments. The Enterprise plan includes ERP integration, dedicated account management, and advanced reporting for complex procurement needs.
FAQ.q6: How does Mdmak Tech ensure supplier quality?
FAQ.a6: All suppliers undergo a verification process including commercial registration (CR) and tax certificate validation. The platform also features a rating and review system where contractors rate suppliers after each completed order, building a transparent reputation system.

Privacy.title: Privacy Policy
Privacy.intro: Mdmak Tech is committed to protecting your privacy and ensuring the security of your personal and commercial data. This privacy policy has been prepared to explain how we collect, use, and protect your information in accordance with the Personal Data Protection Law in Saudi Arabia and global best practices.
Privacy.sec1_desc: When using the Mdmak Tech platform, we collect the following types of information:
Privacy.sec1_list_1: Basic Information: Name, email, job title, contact number, and Commercial Registration (CR).
Privacy.sec1_list_2: Company Data: Company information, commercial registration, procurement details, and RFQ data.
Privacy.sec1_list_3: Technical Data: IP address, browser type, and device information used to access the platform.
Privacy.sec2_desc: We use your data for the following purposes:
Privacy.sec2_list_1: To provide, operate, and maintain the Mdmak Tech platform to facilitate construction procurement.
Privacy.sec2_list_2: To improve user experience and develop new features that meet the needs of the contracting sector.
Privacy.sec2_list_3: To communicate with you regarding updates, security alerts, and technical support.
Privacy.sec2_list_4: To comply with legal and regulatory requirements in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.
Privacy.sec3_desc_1: We do not sell your personal data to any third parties. RFQ-related data is only shared between relevant parties (contractors and suppliers) based on the access permissions you set.
Privacy.sec3_desc_2: We use industry-leading encryption protocols (SSL/TLS) to protect your data during transmission and storage. Our servers are hosted in data centers that comply with local security requirements (e.g., National Cybersecurity Authority NCA).
Privacy.sec4_title: 4. Your Rights as a Data Subject
Privacy.sec4_desc: According to local regulations, you have the right to:
Privacy.sec4_list_1: Access and view your personal data.
Privacy.sec4_list_2: Request corrections or updates to your information.
Privacy.sec4_list_3: Request the deletion of your data (as permitted by commercial regulations).
Privacy.sec5_desc: If you have any questions about our privacy policy or how we process your data, please contact our privacy team at:

Shared.sset_desc: What the Sales module owns, what it reads from others, and what will never be built here
Shared.sset_step_1_body: Arrives from CRM only: a quote request for a client or prospect registered there. There is no direct door — a new party is registered in CRM first.
Shared.sset_step_1_guard: A request past its due date shows red · what we cannot price goes back with a factual reason — never an apology.
Shared.sset_step_2_body: Price comes from the client agreement, then the quantity tier, then the list; lead time from honest readiness. None of that lives in CRM, so pricing happens here — one record, not two copies.
Shared.sset_step_2_guard: A discount above the role's cap is blocked · selling below cost is blocked for every role.
Shared.sset_step_3_body: You type in the form and it appears at once on an official document under the company's letterhead and VAT number — lines, discount, amount in words, payment schedule and terms — printable or saved as PDF. Then you log that it was sent, and validity starts.
Shared.sset_step_3_guard: Issuing locks the figures · sending locks the whole document · any later change is a revision carrying the base number and a suffix.
Shared.sset_step_4_body: The client's acceptance turns the quote into an order with a frozen price and a delivery promise. The opportunity closes as won in CRM, and the win rate is computed from quote outcomes, never typed.
Shared.sset_step_4_guard: No order without an accepted quote · the promise is never earlier than the earliest honest readiness.
Shared.sset_step_5_body: Written in the quote and carried to the order as the client accepted it: instalments with their percentages. Anything made to order is not quoted without an advance before production — the same rule Manufacturing enforces.
Shared.sset_step_5_guard: No invoice and no receipt here · the advance blocks reservation and execution until Finance confirms the deposit — not until the client says "I paid".
Shared.sset_step_6_body: When you report the advance to Finance, the production request for the shortfall reaches the plant as "awaiting Finance": it plans but does not execute. Once Finance confirms, the plant answers with a work order or a reasoned decline.
Shared.sset_step_6_guard: No reservation or execution before Finance confirms the advance · the plant's response clock starts after confirmation.
Shared.sset_step_7_body: A made-to-measure product does not enter production before the measurement is recorded, and a drawn product is not cut before the client approves. Manufacturing records the measurement and we only nudge; the client's approval is ours to chase and record.
Shared.sset_step_7_guard: While either gate is closed, readiness is not computed at all.
Shared.sset_step_8_body: The work order moves through the stations, and what is finished enters the warehouse as stock that Inventory owns.
Shared.sset_step_8_guard: Scheduling and priority are the plant's call — we read the ready date and never book capacity.
Shared.sset_step_9_body: The three-step handshake: issue request → Inventory authorises → the client signs for the quantity actually received, which may differ from the request — and value follows it.
Shared.sset_step_9_guard: A quantity above truly-available stock is blocked · a shipment held by Finance does not leave until released.
Shared.sset_step_10_body: When the client tells you they paid an instalment, you report it to Finance with the amount, transfer date, bank reference and the receipt if there is one. That is your whole part in the money.
Shared.sset_step_10_guard: We issue no invoice and record no receipt · nothing changes on the order before Finance answers.
Shared.sset_step_11_body: Finance matches the deposit against the bank statement and answers: confirmed, or not found — the tax invoice and its posting are theirs alone.
Shared.sset_step_11_guard: "Not found" returns to us as a decision: check with the client and report again · "confirmed" on the advance releases the order.
Shared.sset_step_12_body: A return with its reason and disposition (back to stock, or scrapped); Finance settles it with a credit note.
Shared.sset_step_12_guard: No return on an unsigned shipment — the delivered quantity is corrected instead of inventing a return.
Shared.sset_rule_body: A module owns the record whose lifecycle it owns. The quote and its document, the order, the promise, the delivery and the transfer notice are Sales' · the invoice, verifying the deposit and the posting are Finance's · the request, the client and the opportunity are CRM's · scheduling and measurement are Manufacturing's · stock and its movement are Inventory's · company details and logo are Settings & Governance's. Whatever you see here from another module carries its source badge and is never edited from here.
Shared.sset_rule_names: A shared name: our "quote request" is inbound from a client and we answer it with a quote — Procurement's "RFQ" is outbound to suppliers and receives offers. Same name, opposite direction.
Shared.sset_boundary_sub: A module owns the record whose lifecycle it owns
Shared.sset_notown_head: Not owned — will not be built here, even if asked

info.incoming: Procurement follows up until delivery is complete; it never confirms receipt. Whoever stands at the delivery point records it — the storekeeper or the site engineer — counting line by line and giving the reason for any reject. No single person both picks the supplier and its price and confirms its goods arrived, and Finance pays only what was accepted. The supplier's notice reaches us first, and when its date falls after the supplier's promise we know the delay before it happens.
info.log: Every receipt — accepted, rejected and short of the supplier's notice, who recorded it and where the material went. A receipt is never edited after recording; a correction is a later receipt or a return to the supplier.
info.nopo: Goods that arrived with no purchase order: the receiver recorded them (nobody turns a waiting truck away), and they wait for us to attach a retroactive order — until then Finance holds the invoice as "no PO".

notes.drift: Impact = (this PO's price − the last price we paid for the same material in the same unit) × quantity. Positive is not always wrong — steel and copper move — but it deserves to be seen.

An advance is due now until Finance records it paid on the order; what Finance paid against invoices comes off "received". "Received" counts the accepted only.
notes.saving: Saving = for each awarded line, (the average unit price quoted by the offers still in the running − the awarded price) × its quantity; where no offer quoted unit prices, the average offer − what we awarded. Positive = saved.
notes.commitmentsTerms: Terms are read from our supplier record first, then the offer's credit days, then days written on the order.

step6.desc: Prepared by one hand, approved by another, then sent

step8.title: Delivery & receipt

step9.title: Invoice & payment
step9.desc: Finance matches the invoice to the order and the receipt, then pays

flow.title: Need to payment — nine steps, one owner each

step1.title: 1 · The need
step1.desc: An approved material request from a project · a workshop shortfall on a work order · a stock gap
step1.rule: We never create the need — it reaches us

step2.title: 2 · Stock check
step2.desc: Computed on arrival and confirmed by Inventory: what we hold free is issued, not bought

step3.title: 3 · Make or buy
step3.desc: What our workshop makes, we ask it first — it accepts in full, in part, or declines with a reason

step4.title: 4 · The path
step4.desc: Live agreement → an order at its price · under the cap → a direct order · otherwise → an RFQ

step5.title: 5 · Quotes & award
step5.desc: Our suppliers · platform suppliers · a guest link with no registration — sealed until close, awarded line by line
step5.rule: A non-lowest award carries its reason

step6.title: 6 · Purchase order
step6.desc: Prepared by one, approved by another within his limit — then sent, with the supplier's acceptance and date recorded
step6.rule: Pending sample, expired CR or no VAT number = no approval

step7.title: 7 · Finance
step7.desc: The approved order reaches Finance as a commitment and the first leg of the match — it pays any advance the supplier asked for
step7.rule: We never pay nor record a payment

step8.title: 8 · Delivery & receipt
step8.desc: We follow the supplier's date — Inventory receives in the store or directly on site and records the quantity and the rejects

step9.title: 9 · Invoice & payment
step9.desc: Finance matches the invoice to our order and Inventory's receipt, and pays — its payment closes the order. A price variance comes back to us as a decision
step9.rule: The price variance is our call

backbone.title: The need line is the backbone
backbone.body: No RFQ or PO is typed from scratch: both are built from lines that reached us. And every quantity lives in one place: from stock + made + awaiting purchase + in offers + on an order + cancelled = what was asked for.

lastDay.title: Last order day
lastDay.body: Need date − lead time − the RFQ cycle. We sort the work by it, because the line that arrived yesterday may be more urgent than one that arrived a week ago.

owns.title: What the module owns
owns.body: The supplier master, price agreements and price history · the path decision and the make-or-buy decision · the RFQ, the recorded offer, the comparison, the award and its reason · the purchase order, its approval, its revisions and the cancellation of its remainder · following the supplier's date · the decision on rejects and on a price variance · the reference price Manufacturing reads.

link.title: The integration contract — what reaches us and what we send
link.sub: We request and read state — never act for another module

pm.in: The approved material request (its purchase part) with item, quantity, date and destination · the item's sample status · the item's remaining budget · the site receipt (counted, rejected with reason) · "stop what has not arrived" when the material is closed
pm.out: Each part's state: offers → made → PO → part arrived → received · the PO number and price as a commitment on the item · the supplier's date and its updates · confirmation that the remainder is cancelled
pm.late: Sample not approved: we collect offers but issue no order · budget overrun undecided: the order waits "on the budget decision"

mfg.in: A purchase request for a work order's shortfall (material, quantity, "needed before") · the workshop's make-or-buy answer · a request to claim from a supplier for waste or a quality report on a block
mfg.out: A project need we decided to make, with its material request and item · the reference purchase price of each product · the arrival date of the requested material
mfg.late: No answer within a day: we go on to buy, and their request closes "moved to purchase"

inv.in: The stock check (what is issued and what is left to buy) · a shortfall at issue · a gap before the need · the receipt: counted, accepted, rejected with reason, held for inspection and its result · a receipt with no PO
inv.out: The approved PO with its lines, supplier, date and destination ("on its way to you") · date updates · cancelling the remainder
inv.late: No stock-check confirmation within a day: we proceed on what was computed · a receipt more than 5% over the order: Inventory refuses it and asks us to amend the order

fin.in: A notice of every payment on our order: the voucher · which invoice · net, VAT and advance recovery · value date · bank reference and the last four digits of the supplier's account · who approved it · the transfer copy — and its share of the order · every payment hold with its coded reason · approval limits and the direct-order cap
fin.out: The approved PO: the first leg of the three-way match and a commitment not yet invoiced · a request for a supplier advance · our decision on a price variance (a revised order or a refusal) · the supplier master, VAT number and payment terms
fin.keys: proc:PO:[PO no.] · proc:ADV:[request no.] · proc:FRJ:[hold no.] · fin:PAY:[voucher] · fin:REJ:[hold no.]
fin.late: An order that never reached Finance: its invoice is held "no PO" · an advance not paid: the supplier's lead time has not started and the honest date slips

sup.in: An offer (from his platform account · from the guest link with no registration · or recorded by the buyer) · a query · acceptance of the order and its date · a delivery notice per shipment: lines, quantities, date, driver and paper note number
sup.out: The RFQ and its link · the answer to a query, to every invitee · a reduction request with a target price · the PO with its link, place and receiver · the receipt result: accepted, rejected with reason, outstanding (what he may invoice)
sup.keys: Guest-link token per RFQ · sup:ASN:[notice no.]
sup.late: The system does not message the supplier beyond the portal and the order: it copies the text and the link, your own tool sends it, and we log that it was sent

never.item1: Recording receipts and their report — whoever receives does: Inventory for its stores, Projects for its sites
never.item2: The invoice, the match, the payment and the supplier ledger — Finance
never.item3: Creating the need or changing its quantity — its owner in Projects or Manufacturing
never.item4: The subcontract and its certificates — Projects
never.item5: Approving a sample — the consultant, through Projects (we only ask the supplier for it)
never.item6: Site petty cash under the cap — Projects and Finance (ours is a direct order with no offers, never cash)
never.item7: The item card, its code and unit — Inventory
never.item8: Messaging suppliers by WhatsApp or e-mail from inside the system

notBuilt.item1: An "urgent buy" on a phoned approval documented within 24 hours — instead of finding out after the pour
notBuilt.item2: A delegate approver when the limit-holder is away
notBuilt.item3: A second sealed round after the prices are opened
notBuilt.item4: A cumulative direct-order cap (material × supplier × project × 30 days) — today there is the per-supplier split window
notBuilt.item5: Returning materials to a supplier after acceptance — with a debit note in Finance
notBuilt.item6: Temporary-labour supply contracts (Ajeer) referred by HR
notBuilt.item7: Timed equipment rental (daily / monthly) and its extension
notBuilt.item9: Supplier pre-qualification by documents and criteria before inviting him

conflict.item1: Inventory calls our document a "purchase request" (ش-…); Finance and Projects call it a purchase order (ط.ش-…). We adopt the latter: the request is what reaches us, the order is what we issue.
conflict.item2: Manufacturing reads «ط.ش» as a purchase request that precedes it — we have no intermediate document: the need line carries the material request number itself.
conflict.item3: Finance expects the receipt number «ا.س-…» and Inventory numbers it «إد-…». We read it in Finance's form.
conflict.item4: Supplier returns: Inventory sends a debit note to Finance, and Finance expects it from us. Correct: Inventory moves the stock, we agree with the supplier, Finance issues the note.
conflict.item5: Projects says Procurement registers an uncatalogued item, yet the item card is Inventory's. Here: it is bought as free text for direct supply, and if it enters a store Inventory registers it at receipt.
conflict.item6: Supplier names differ between Projects, Inventory and Finance. The supplier master here is the reference.
conflict.item7: «ط.ع» is a customer's inbound request in Sales and a labour request in HR — so our outbound RFQ to suppliers is numbered «ع.ش».
conflict.item8: Procurement's chip is violet in two modules and teal in three. Every module now takes its own colour from the registry.

help.title: Why sections are switched off
help.intro: An O&M contract needs no critical path; a self-build needs no certificates. A section that is off is not just hidden — its decisions, alerts and figures go with it, so the project is not measured by what is not its business.
help.confirm_note: What it holds in count and riyals, and what goes silent — then a reason recorded in your name
help.money_note: Stock balance · plant on site · subcontractor dues · uncollected certificate
help.paper_note: Blocking everything drives people to workarounds worse than switching off
help.nothing_note: Switching back restores the data and decisions as they were

recon.more: {qty} more than expected — a saving, or unmeasured work.

recon.due_title: Recoveries awaiting deduction from the next certificate

bound.title: Module boundary
bound.sub: We request and read state — never act for another module, nor mediate between two
bound.own: The project and its acceptance · contract items and budget · measurement and progress · variations · the certificate up to the consultant's certification · sub certificates · material requests, change decisions and technical approval · the project store: receipt on site, use, returns, moves and losses · submittals · inspections and punch · programme and claims · provisional and final handover · the project team · contract terms and their addenda after signature (the original stays)
bound.read: Main-store stock, what is free of it, issue authorisation and returns received (Inventory) · the plant register, its calendar, meters, licences and maintenance · quotes, award, purchase order and make-or-buy (Procurement) · invoice, collection, payments, retention received and actual cost from the ledger (Finance) · the client and the handover file (CRM) · roles and approval limits (Governance)
bound.send: Keyed events to Finance (the table below) · the approved material request goes undivided to Procurement alone, which asks Inventory · “stop what has not arrived” · receipt proof on the project to whoever delivered · return requests · non-conforming material to the supplier · approved losses, inter-project moves and signed addenda to Finance. Resending never produces a second entry.
bound.never_title: Never done for them, whoever asks
bound.never: RFQ, award, purchase-order cancellation and supplier returns · issuing from the main store and receiving returns there · invoicing, collection and retention claims · ordering straight from the workshop (it goes through Procurement) · attendance and payroll · chat channels

bound.conf_sub: need unifying in governance — not ours to fix

conf.amd: Finance has no contract-amendment event. A signed addendum reaches it as its own event prj:AMD:<project>:<n> with the changed financial terms — never a second advance event, to avoid booking it twice. Finance must define it and apply it going forward.
conf.ipc_books: Finance does not yet read the pmEvents outbox: certified certificates, handovers and approved budgets are sent here and wait for it.
conf.sub_commit: Registering a subcontract commits its value here at once, but Finance only learns of it at the first approved certificate. A commitment entry on signing would be a new event needing a governance decision.
conf.loss_move: Two events for Finance are not in its integration contract: approved losses (a cost on the item) and material moved between projects (its cost moves with it).
conf.hnd_units: Finance allows one handover event per project and type — delivery units handed over one by one would need the unit in the key.
conf.crm_creates: CRM says the handover “creates a project” — it delivers a handover file to New projects; the project is created when the receiving manager accepts it, or it is redirected or returned.
conf.crm_months: The contract duration is in months in CRM's handover form, in days here and in the programme.
conf.store_twice: The project store is now a ledger PM owns (receipt on site, use, returns, moves, losses); Inventory still keeps site stores and write-offs for the same thing — Inventory should keep the main stores only.
conf.prefix: «أ.ت» is our variation and «أت» the workshop's work order — nearly identical prefixes for two different documents.
